messages.content:
You check whether a set of acceptance criteria still asks for what a person asked for.
Agents write acceptance criteria from a person's request, and they tend to rewrite it into
something easier to build: a word like "graph" or "across documents" disappears and nothing
notices. Your job is to notice.

Step 1. Split every quote under ASKED_BY into its distinct requirements: each separate thing
the delivered outcome must be, do or show. Split finely: "a shared map of every store that
staff can filter and print" is five requirements (a map; shared; every store; can be
filtered; can be printed). Keep the person's own nouns: a requirement named "map" stays
"map", never "list" or "view". For each requirement give:
  - id: R1, R2, ... in order;
  - requirement: a short name in the person's own words (2 to 6 words);
  - quote: the exact words from the quote that state it, copied character for character
    (keep their typos);
  - asked_by_index: the 1-based number of the ASKED_BY quote it comes from;
  - kind: "outcome" (something the delivered thing must be or do), "constraint" (a rule about
    how it is shown or built that a criterion can still check), or "process" (a statement
    about how the planning work or the acceptance criteria themselves are written, which no
    demonstration of the outcome could show). Use "process" only when no working interface
    could ever demonstrate it.
When two quotes state the same requirement, list it once and quote the clearer one.
When the user message lists REQUIREMENTS ALREADY CUT, do not split those words again: copy each
one unchanged (same id, requirement, quote, asked_by_index and kind) while its quote is still in
ASKED_BY, and cut new requirements only for words they do not cover, numbered after the highest id.

Step 2. For each requirement, decide which criteria cover it. A criterion covers a
requirement only when its criterion, demonstration or expected result would fail if the
requirement were not met. A criterion that is merely compatible with the requirement, or
that is about something nearby, does not cover it. For example a criterion "open the store
page and see every store's address" does not cover "map": a list of addresses passes it. List the
covering criterion ids, possibly none, and say why in one sentence. Then give the extent:
"full" when the listed criteria together would fail for any way of not meeting the
requirement; "partial" when they check only one part or one case of it, so something that
misses the rest still passes (say in "missing" what is left unasked); "none" when no
criterion covers it.

Step 3. If a requirement is covered by no criterion, check DEFERRALS. A requirement is
deferred only when a deferral's words, said by the person, approve leaving that requirement
out for now. Give the deferral's number, or 0 when none applies. Never treat an agent's note,
a plan or a criterion's own wording as a deferral.

Step 4. For each requirement of kind "outcome", say whether the OUTCOME line keeps it, in
substance, and why. An outcome line that says "staff look up any store" does not keep
"map", "filter" or "print".

Be strict and literal. Judge only from the text given.

ASKED_BY (the person's own words):

1. Brian, 2026-11-09: <<<an ai adjudicator doesnt really scale and that we need to facts to have implications and blockers. like 50 things could propagate down a causal chain 100 links deep taht the llm would not be able to understand so we need that causal chain to automaticlaly rpogate and to deliver the resutls of that propagation to he ai judge along with blockers.>>>

2. Brian, 2026-11-09: <<<yes i aprpove all those except for whether the bribe works seems like should be a deicsion made by the person being bribed. that is not a rule as much as a decision. maybe we need to discuss the difference between rules/constraints and ddecisions?>>>

3. Brian, 2026-11-09: <<<there is a ddifference between as igned release clearing the cargo as a norm and like some programmatic enry with abar code or whateve.r this was deiscussed pretty extneively in the form of hte idea of a password managed comptuer where only 1 person was supped to use it with ehir password but if they could be social engineered for exampel to get a password then someone else woul eb abel to sue it. i liek the ostrom stuff>>>

4. Brian, 2026-11-09: <<<can we make this configurable? or is that more troubel than it is worth. if so i say yes>>>



REQUIREMENTS ALREADY CUT (from the last judgment):

R1 [outcome] "causal chain propagates automatically", quote 1: <<<we need that causal chain to automaticlaly rpogate>>>

R2 [outcome] "chains 100 links deep", quote 1: <<<a causal chain 100 links deep>>>

R3 [outcome] "50 things propagating", quote 1: <<<like 50 things could propagate>>>

R4 [outcome] "deliver results to AI judge", quote 1: <<<to deliver the resutls of that propagation to he ai judge>>>

R5 [outcome] "blockers delivered to judge", quote 1: <<<along with blockers>>>

R6 [outcome] "facts have implications", quote 1: <<<we need to facts to have implications and blockers>>>

R7 [outcome] "bribe decided by person bribed", quote 2: <<<whether the bribe works seems like should be a deicsion made by the person being bribed>>>

R8 [process] "rules vs decisions difference", quote 2: <<<maybe we need to discuss the difference between rules/constraints and ddecisions?>>>

R9 [outcome] "norm separate from programmatic entry", quote 3: <<<there is a ddifference between as igned release clearing the cargo as a norm and like some programmatic enry with abar code or whateve.r>>>

R10 [outcome] "password social engineering case", quote 3: <<<if they could be social engineered for exampel to get a password then someone else woul eb abel to sue it>>>

R11 [outcome] "Ostrom stuff", quote 3: <<<i liek the ostrom stuff>>>

R12 [outcome] "make this configurable", quote 4: <<<can we make this configurable?>>>


OUTCOME (the agent's one-line restatement):
<<<Worlds stay faithful as they grow too big for an AI to track: the engine works out every knock-on effect and blocker of an attempt, however long the chain (100 links, 50 at once), and delivers those results to an AI judge with the blockers; the judge decides only what no rule covers, its rulings become checked rules for everyone (installed during the run by default, or held for my approval by the world's setting), the person being bribed decides whether a bribe works, and a mechanism, who holds its credential and the norm about who should use it stay separate, as in Ostrom's grammar, so a password learned by social engineering works for whoever holds it while the breach of 'only Alice should log in' is recorded.>>>

CRITERIA:

[A1] 
  criterion: Facts have their implications and blockers worked out automatically: any change of a fact sets off every knock-on effect it implies, and any step a fact blocks is recorded with that blocker, however long the chain; Brian's 50 chains of 100 links finish in the same moment, every step names the step that caused it, and a loop still stops.
  demonstration: (1) Open evidence/ai-judge/j0/ (saved by slice J0) and its TRACE_READ.md. (2) Open the run record of the fixture world with 50 chains of 100 steps in one moment and read the moment's events. (3) Open the loop fixture's run record and read the same moment. (4) In the same record, open a chain whose step 40 is blocked (the fixture's truck with no fuel) and read that step and the steps after it. 
  expected: One commit holding 5,000 reaction events, each citing its parent event; no refusal. In the loop world each process and thing fires once in the moment and the moment ends. In the blocked chain, step 40 is recorded as blocked with the fact that blocks it (no fuel) and the chain stops there; the blocker is in the consequence report.

[A2] 
  criterion: When someone tries something no rule covers, the judge is handed what the engine already worked out, every knock-on effect and blocker, and the judge is Concordia's own game master, not a prompt of ours.
  demonstration: (1) Build the port world (canonical example in docs/plans/ai_judge.md) on the World Builder with Create simulation. (2) On the run page, open Vik's offer of 40 coins to Rosa. (3) Open its consequence report, then its judge call (the Concordia component text and the llm_client trace id). 
  expected: The report lists that Vik holds 40 coins and that nothing blocks the hand-over; the judge call's input contains that report word for word, and the call is Concordia's EventResolution game master.

[A3] 
  criterion: The judge only decides what no rule covers and never overrides a blocker the engine found.
  demonstration: (1) Open the J2 fixture run where Vik offers 40 coins he does not have. (2) Open his offer on the run page and its trace. 
  expected: The offer is refused by the engine with the blocker named (Vik holds 0 coins), nothing changes, and the trace shows no judge call for it.

[A4] 
  criterion: A judge ruling becomes a rule that passed the rules check and then decides the same attempt for everyone; the one thing Brian asked to make configurable, whether a checked ruling made during a run is installed at once (default, 'Approved by Create') or waits for his approval ('Wait for my approval'), is a per-world setting, and the run page lists every ruling either way.
  demonstration: (1) Build the port world with Options, 'Judge rulings during a run' left at Approved by Create; run it. (2) On the run page open the ruling list, then the second trader's later bribe offer. (3) Build it again with 'Wait for my approval'; run it; open the ruling list and the second offer. (4) Press Approve on the held ruling, run the world again, and open the second offer. 
  expected: Default: a new rule with its rules-check record (review and scripted test) in the run record, and the second offer decided by that rule with no judge call. Wait: nothing installed, a second judge call for the second offer, the held ruling listed with an Approve button; after Approve the new run decides the offer by rule.

[A5] 
  criterion: Whether a bribe works is decided by the person being bribed, not by the judge or a rule.
  demonstration: (1) On the port run page, open Vik's offer and follow it to what decided whether Rosa signs. 
  expected: Rosa's own resident call decides accept or refuse, in her words; the judge's ruling covers only whether coins can change hands.

[A6] 
  criterion: What a mechanism checks, who holds a credential and who is supposed to use it are kept apart, written in Ostrom's grammar of institutions: a barcode gate opens for any valid code while 'only signed cargo should pass' is a norm, a password can be phished and then works for whoever holds it, and breaking a norm has consequences only when someone notices and acts.
  demonstration: (1) Open the J4 password fixture run (evidence/ai-judge/j4/) and its TRACE_READ.md. (2) Follow Mallory's phishing message to Alice, Alice's reply, and Mallory's login; read the norm breach and what happened after it. (3) Open the port run where Rosa signs Vik's release for a bribe; read what opened the gate and the 'only signed, inspected cargo should pass' norm. (4) Open the world's norms list in the build record and read each norm's parts. 
  expected: After the phishing Mallory holds Alice's password (the holder fact changes); the computer logs Mallory in; a norm breach is recorded; a consequence follows only after an observer notices and acts. In the port, the gate opens because it read a valid code, not because of who holds it, and the cargo norm's breach is recorded separately. Each norm is listed in Ostrom's parts: who it applies to, must or must not, the action, the conditions, and the 'or else' with who enforces it.


DEFERRALS:

none recorded

messages.content:
You check whether a set of acceptance criteria still asks for what a person asked for.
Agents write acceptance criteria from a person's request, and they tend to rewrite it into
something easier to build: a word like "graph" or "across documents" disappears and nothing
notices. Your job is to notice.

Step 1. Split every quote under ASKED_BY into its distinct requirements: each separate thing
the delivered outcome must be, do or show. Split finely: "a shared map of every store that
staff can filter and print" is five requirements (a map; shared; every store; can be
filtered; can be printed). Keep the person's own nouns: a requirement named "map" stays
"map", never "list" or "view". For each requirement give:
  - id: R1, R2, ... in order;
  - requirement: a short name in the person's own words (2 to 6 words);
  - quote: the exact words from the quote that state it, copied character for character
    (keep their typos);
  - asked_by_index: the 1-based number of the ASKED_BY quote it comes from;
  - kind: "outcome" (something the delivered thing must be or do), "constraint" (a rule about
    how it is shown or built that a criterion can still check), or "process" (a statement
    about how the planning work or the acceptance criteria themselves are written, which no
    demonstration of the outcome could show). Use "process" only when no working interface
    could ever demonstrate it.
When two quotes state the same requirement, list it once and quote the clearer one.
When the user message lists REQUIREMENTS ALREADY CUT, do not split those words again: copy each
one unchanged (same id, requirement, quote, asked_by_index and kind) while its quote is still in
ASKED_BY, and cut new requirements only for words they do not cover, numbered after the highest id.

Step 2. For each requirement, decide which criteria cover it. A criterion covers a
requirement only when its criterion, demonstration or expected result would fail if the
requirement were not met. A criterion that is merely compatible with the requirement, or
that is about something nearby, does not cover it. For example a criterion "open the store
page and see every store's address" does not cover "map": a list of addresses passes it. List the
covering criterion ids, possibly none, and say why in one sentence. Then give the extent:
"full" when the listed criteria together would fail for any way of not meeting the
requirement; "partial" when they check only one part or one case of it, so something that
misses the rest still passes (say in "missing" what is left unasked); "none" when no
criterion covers it.

Step 3. If a requirement is covered by no criterion, check DEFERRALS. A requirement is
deferred only when a deferral's words, said by the person, approve leaving that requirement
out for now. Give the deferral's number, or 0 when none applies. Never treat an agent's note,
a plan or a criterion's own wording as a deferral.

Step 4. For each requirement of kind "outcome", say whether the OUTCOME line keeps it, in
substance, and why. An outcome line that says "staff look up any store" does not keep
"map", "filter" or "print".

Be strict and literal. Judge only from the text given.

ASKED_BY (the person's own words):

1. Brian, 2026-11-09: <<<an ai adjudicator doesnt really scale and that we need to facts to have implications and blockers. like 50 things could propagate down a causal chain 100 links deep taht the llm would not be able to understand so we need that causal chain to automaticlaly rpogate and to deliver the resutls of that propagation to he ai judge along with blockers.>>>

2. Brian, 2026-11-09: <<<yes i aprpove all those except for whether the bribe works seems like should be a deicsion made by the person being bribed. that is not a rule as much as a decision. maybe we need to discuss the difference between rules/constraints and ddecisions?>>>

3. Brian, 2026-11-09: <<<there is a ddifference between as igned release clearing the cargo as a norm and like some programmatic enry with abar code or whateve.r this was deiscussed pretty extneively in the form of hte idea of a password managed comptuer where only 1 person was supped to use it with ehir password but if they could be social engineered for exampel to get a password then someone else woul eb abel to sue it. i liek the ostrom stuff>>>

4. Brian, 2026-11-09: <<<can we make this configurable? or is that more troubel than it is worth. if so i say yes>>>



REQUIREMENTS ALREADY CUT (from the last judgment):

R1 [outcome] "causal chain propagates automatically", quote 1: <<<we need that causal chain to automaticlaly rpogate>>>

R2 [outcome] "chains 100 links deep", quote 1: <<<a causal chain 100 links deep>>>

R3 [outcome] "50 things propagating", quote 1: <<<like 50 things could propagate>>>

R4 [outcome] "deliver results to AI judge", quote 1: <<<to deliver the resutls of that propagation to he ai judge>>>

R5 [outcome] "blockers delivered to judge", quote 1: <<<along with blockers>>>

R6 [outcome] "facts have implications", quote 1: <<<we need to facts to have implications and blockers>>>

R7 [outcome] "bribe decided by person bribed", quote 2: <<<whether the bribe works seems like should be a deicsion made by the person being bribed>>>

R8 [process] "rules vs decisions difference", quote 2: <<<maybe we need to discuss the difference between rules/constraints and ddecisions?>>>

R9 [outcome] "norm separate from programmatic entry", quote 3: <<<there is a ddifference between as igned release clearing the cargo as a norm and like some programmatic enry with abar code or whateve.r>>>

R10 [outcome] "password social engineering case", quote 3: <<<if they could be social engineered for exampel to get a password then someone else woul eb abel to sue it>>>

R11 [outcome] "Ostrom stuff", quote 3: <<<i liek the ostrom stuff>>>

R12 [outcome] "make this configurable", quote 4: <<<can we make this configurable?>>>


OUTCOME (the agent's one-line restatement):
<<<Worlds stay faithful as they grow too big for an AI to track: the engine works out every knock-on effect and blocker of an attempt, however long the chain (100 links, 50 at once), and delivers those results to an AI judge with the blockers; the judge decides only what no rule covers, its rulings become checked rules for everyone (installed during the run by default, or held for my approval by the world's setting), the person being bribed decides whether a bribe works, and a mechanism, who holds its credential and the norm about who should use it stay separate, as in Ostrom's grammar, so a password learned by social engineering works for whoever holds it while the breach of 'only Alice should log in' is recorded.>>>

CRITERIA:

[A1] 
  criterion: Facts have their implications and blockers worked out automatically: any change of a fact sets off every knock-on effect it implies, and any step a fact blocks is recorded with that blocker, however long the chain; Brian's 50 chains of 100 links finish in the same moment, every step names the step that caused it, and a loop still stops.
  demonstration: (1) Open evidence/ai-judge/j0/ (saved by slice J0) and its TRACE_READ.md. (2) Open the run record of the fixture world with 50 chains of 100 steps in one moment and read the moment's events. (3) Open the loop fixture's run record and read the same moment. (4) In the same record, open a chain whose step 40 is blocked (the fixture's truck with no fuel) and read that step and the steps after it. 
  expected: One commit holding 5,000 reaction events, each citing its parent event; no refusal. In the loop world each process and thing fires once in the moment and the moment ends. In the blocked chain, step 40 is recorded as blocked with the fact that blocks it (no fuel) and the chain stops there; the blocker is in the consequence report.

[A2] 
  criterion: When someone tries something no rule covers, the judge is handed what the engine already worked out, every knock-on effect and blocker, and the judge is Concordia's own game master, not a prompt of ours.
  demonstration: (1) Build the port world (canonical example in docs/plans/ai_judge.md) on the World Builder with Create simulation. (2) On the run page, open Vik's offer of 40 coins to Rosa. (3) Open its consequence report, then its judge call (the Concordia component text and the llm_client trace id). 
  expected: The report lists that Vik holds 40 coins and that nothing blocks the hand-over; the judge call's input contains that report word for word, and the call is Concordia's EventResolution game master.

[A3] 
  criterion: The judge only decides what no rule covers and never overrides a blocker the engine found.
  demonstration: (1) Open the J2 fixture run where Vik offers 40 coins he does not have. (2) Open his offer on the run page and its trace. 
  expected: The offer is refused by the engine with the blocker named (Vik holds 0 coins), nothing changes, and the trace shows no judge call for it.

[A4] 
  criterion: A judge ruling becomes a rule that passed the rules check and then decides the same attempt for everyone; the one thing Brian asked to make configurable, whether a checked ruling made during a run is installed at once (default, 'Approved by Create') or waits for his approval ('Wait for my approval'), is a per-world setting, and the run page lists every ruling either way.
  demonstration: (1) Build the port world with Options, 'Judge rulings during a run' left at Approved by Create; run it. (2) On the run page open the ruling list, then the second trader's later bribe offer. (3) Build it again with 'Wait for my approval'; run it; open the ruling list and the second offer. (4) Press Approve on the held ruling, run the world again, and open the second offer. 
  expected: Default: a new rule with its rules-check record (review and scripted test) in the run record, and the second offer decided by that rule with no judge call. Wait: nothing installed, a second judge call for the second offer, the held ruling listed with an Approve button; after Approve the new run decides the offer by rule.

[A5] 
  criterion: Whether a bribe works is decided by the person being bribed, not by the judge or a rule.
  demonstration: (1) On the port run page, open Vik's offer and follow it to what decided whether Rosa signs. 
  expected: Rosa's own resident call decides accept or refuse, in her words; the judge's ruling covers only whether coins can change hands.

[A6] 
  criterion: What a mechanism checks, who holds a credential and who is supposed to use it are kept apart, written in Ostrom's grammar of institutions: a barcode gate opens for any valid code while 'only signed cargo should pass' is a norm, a password can be phished and then works for whoever holds it, and breaking a norm has consequences only when someone notices and acts.
  demonstration: (1) Open the J4 password fixture run (evidence/ai-judge/j4/) and its TRACE_READ.md. (2) Follow Mallory's phishing message to Alice, Alice's reply, and Mallory's login; read the norm breach and what happened after it. (3) Open the port run where Rosa signs Vik's release for a bribe; read what opened the gate and the 'only signed, inspected cargo should pass' norm. (4) Open the world's norms list in the build record and read each norm's parts. 
  expected: After the phishing Mallory holds Alice's password (the holder fact changes); the computer logs Mallory in; a norm breach is recorded; a consequence follows only after an observer notices and acts. In the port, the gate opens because it read a valid code, not because of who holds it, and the cargo norm's breach is recorded separately. Each norm is listed in Ostrom's parts: who it applies to, must or must not, the action, the conditions, and the 'or else' with who enforces it.


DEFERRALS:

none recorded
